# `raptorbt.pricing`

European option pricing, Greeks and implied volatility.

Two models, both lognormal:

``"black_scholes"``
    ``underlying`` is a spot price. The forward is ``S * exp((rate - dividend_yield) * tau)``
    (Black-Scholes-Merton with a continuous dividend or carry yield).
``"black76"``
    ``underlying`` is already a forward (a futures price); no carry is applied, the rate only
    discounts the premium, and ``dividend_yield`` must be 0.

Every function takes scalars or NumPy-broadcastable arrays. With scalars it returns scalars and
raises ``ValueError`` for inputs no model can price. With arrays it returns arrays and marks any
invalid element ``NaN`` (``NaN`` means absent, never zero); the work runs in Rust, off the GIL,
on all cores for large inputs.

Units: ``tau`` is years (see :func:`year_fraction`); ``vol``, ``rate`` and ``dividend_yield`` are
annual decimals (0.2 = 20%); ``vega`` is per 1.00 of volatility, ``rho`` per 1.00 of rate,
``theta`` per year (negative when the option decays), ``delta`` per unit of ``underlying``.
Divide ``vega`` and ``rho`` by 100 for "per volatility point" and "per 1%", and ``theta`` by 365
for "per calendar day".

Implied volatility never guesses. :func:`implied_vol` raises :class:`ImpliedVolError` (scalar) or
returns ``NaN`` (arrays) when no volatility in ``[lo, hi]`` reproduces the price;
:func:`implied_vol_status` says why, with an :class:`IvStatus`.

See ``docs/pricing.md`` for the numerical assumptions.

### `OptionChain`

*class*

```python
class OptionChain
OptionChain(specs)
```

Option contracts by underlying, expiry and strike, visible only as they
are listed. Every query takes the current event time `now_ns`.

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `atm_strike(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, reference)` | The listed strike nearest `reference` (the lower one on a tie). |
| `atm_strike_forward(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, spot, rate=0.0, dividend_yield=0.0)` | The listed strike nearest the forward of `spot` to this expiry. |
| `by_delta(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, right, target, underlying_price, vol, rate=0.0, dividend_yield=0.0, model='black_scholes')` | The listed contract of `right` whose model delta is nearest `target` (calls positive, puts negative) at a flat `vol`. |
| `closest_by(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, right, target, measure)` | The listed contract of `right` whose `measure(contract)` is nearest `target` (the lower strike on a tie). `measure` returns a number, or None / NaN to skip a contract: a quoted premium, say. |
| `contract(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, strike, right, now_ns)` | The contract at exactly these terms, or None if not listed at `now_ns`. |
| `contracts(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, right=None)` | Contracts of one expiry listed at `now_ns`, by ascending strike. |
| `expiries(self, /, underlying, now_ns)` | Expiries with a contract listed at `now_ns`, ascending. |
| `pick_expiry(self, /, underlying, now_ns, which='nearest', n=0, min_days=0, date_ns=None, utc_offset_ns=0)` | Pick an expiry listed at `now_ns`. `which` is `"nearest"` (first at or after `min_days` days from now), `"nth"` (0 = nearest), `"weekly"` / `"monthly"` (the `n`th that is not / is the last of its calendar month) or `"date"` (the one on the same day as `date_ns`). Months and days follow `utc_offset_ns`. |
| `strike_at_offset(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, reference, offset)` | The strike `offset` listed strikes above the one nearest `reference` (negative: below); None if that runs off the chain. |
| `strikes(self, /, underlying, expiry_ns, now_ns, right=None)` | Strikes listed at `now_ns` for one expiry, ascending; one right if given. |
| `underlyings(self, /)` | *No docstring.* |

### `implied_vol`

*function*

```python
implied_vol(price: 'Any', right: 'Any', underlying: 'Any', strike: 'Any', tau: 'Any', rate: 'Any' = 0.0, dividend_yield: 'Any' = 0.0, *, model: 'str' = 'black_scholes', lo: 'float' = 0.0001, hi: 'float' = 5.0, tol: 'float' = 1e-12, max_iter: 'int' = 200) -> 'Any'
```

The volatility at which the model prices ``price``.

Scalars: returns a float or raises :class:`ImpliedVolError` (its ``status`` says why).
Arrays: returns an array with ``NaN`` wherever there is none; use
:func:`implied_vol_status` to see why. Search is limited to ``[lo, hi]``
(default 0.01% to 500%); a price outside what that range reaches is reported, not clamped.

### `implied_vol_status`

*function*

```python
implied_vol_status(price: 'Any', right: 'Any', underlying: 'Any', strike: 'Any', tau: 'Any', rate: 'Any' = 0.0, dividend_yield: 'Any' = 0.0, *, model: 'str' = 'black_scholes', lo: 'float' = 0.0001, hi: 'float' = 5.0, tol: 'float' = 1e-12, max_iter: 'int' = 200) -> 'tuple[Any, Any]'
```

``(iv, status)``: never raises for a price with no volatility. ``iv`` is ``NaN`` unless
``status`` is :attr:`IvStatus.OK`. A scalar call gives ``(float, IvStatus)``, an array call
``(float64 array, uint8 array of IvStatus codes)``.
